identity.short_description: Tianqi Lithium Corporation is a Chinese, dual-listed (Shenzhen 002466 / Hong Kong 9696) vertically integrated lithium major and one of the world's largest producers of lithium raw materials and lithium chemicals. Its economic activities span hard-rock lithium mining and lithium chemical conversion. Upstream, it controls a 51% interest in Talison Lithium Pty Ltd — operator of the Greenbushes lithium mine in Western Australia, the world's largest and lowest-cost hard-rock (spodumene) lithium operation (Albemarle holds the other 49% of Talison) — held through Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia Pty Ltd (TLEA), a joint venture Tianqi controls at 51% with IGO Limited at 49%. TLEA also owns 100% of the Kwinana battery-grade lithium hydroxide refinery in Western Australia (nameplate 24,000 t/yr Train 1). Domestically Tianqi operates lithium chemical conversion plants at Shehong and Suining Anju (Sichuan), Zhangjiagang (Jiangsu) and Tongliang (Chongqing), with total built lithium chemical capacity of roughly 91,600 t/yr. Tianqi also holds a ~22.16% equity stake in Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. (SQM), one of the world's largest lithium producers (Salar de Atacama brine), acquired in 2018 for USD ~4.1bn. In 2024 Tianqi reported revenue of RMB 13.063bn (down ~67.8% y/y) and a net loss attributable to shareholders of RMB 7.905bn — its most loss-making year since listing — driven by the collapse in lithium prices, weaker SQM results, impairments and FX losses. The controlling shareholder is Chengdu Tianqi Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. (founder/chairman Jiang Weiping).

economic_activities.description: Open-pit mining of spodumene (hard-rock lithium) ore at the Greenbushes operation in Western Australia and beneficiation into technical- and chemical-grade lithium concentrate (spodumene concentrate). Greenbushes is the world's largest and lowest-cost operating hard-rock lithium mine. Conducted through Talison Lithium, jointly owned by TLEA (51%, Tianqi-controlled) and Albemarle (49%). Concentrate is shared as offtake between the two shareholders in proportion to ownership and feeds Tianqi's downstream chemical conversion (including Kwinana and its Chinese plants).

economic_activities.description: Conversion of spodumene concentrate into battery-grade and industrial-grade lithium chemicals — principally lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate, plus lithium chloride and lithium metal. Performed in Australia through TLEA's 100%-owned Kwinana battery-grade lithium hydroxide refinery (nameplate 24,000 t/yr Train 1), and in China through Tianqi's own conversion plants at Shehong and Suining Anju (Sichuan), Zhangjiagang (Jiangsu) and Tongliang (Chongqing), with total built lithium chemical capacity of roughly 91,600 t/yr. Outputs supply the lithium-ion battery and broader industrial value chain.

corporate_vehicles.relationship_description: TLEA owns 100% of the Kwinana battery-grade lithium hydroxide refinery in Western Australia. Kwinana is one of the largest fully automated battery-grade lithium hydroxide facilities globally and the first built in Australia (Train 1 nameplate 24,000 t/yr). The plant has faced ramp-up and viability challenges; Train 2 construction was suspended and IGO impaired its 49% interest in FY25.
